thread:
noah: hey folks, day 1 question. I generated a hosted API key but my streaming tests return 429s sporadically. I thought hosted keys had more quota than sandbox?
onboard-bot: welcome noah! :wave: Sandbox keys = low dev quotas. Hosted keys use org quotas which are higher but still enforce per-route and per-token limits. Check Console -> API Keys to confirm key type.
sara: streaming counts both request-level rate and token emission rate. if you open lots of concurrent streams or large `max_tokens` you can trip the token-rate limiter.
noah: sometimes the 429 has a `Retry-After` header, sometimes not. what should my client do?
infra: always respect `Retry-After` when present. otherwise use exponential backoff with jitter (e.g., 300ms * 2^n + rand(0,250ms), cap ~5s). for streaming specifically, try lowering `max_tokens` or multiplexing fewer concurrent sessions.
noah: is there a quick way to see my sandbox quota while onboarding? I don't see usage in Console yet.
onboard-bot: new hires typically need org mapping to see metrics. file an IT ticket at https://redwood.internal/it-requests with subject "map user to org for quota view" and tag @infra. include your github handle.
sara: for embeddings: sandbox concurrency is low. prefer batches of 8-12 vectors for stable runs. hosted can handle bigger batches but watch overall concurrent requests.
noah: thanks! if I need a short-lived sandbox bump for a demo, who do I ask?
infra: use the onboarding sandbox increase form (pinned in #new-hires) and include dates + estimated request volume. small bumps usually within 12h. hosted increases go through growth/billing (24-48h).
noah: perfect, saved. one last thing: any client pattern to avoid getting surprised by 429s in prod?
sara: implement retries with jitter, respect `Retry-After`, add circuit-breaker after repeated 429s, and configure a fallback model/quantized variant for automatic downgrade. also log 429 contexts (route, concurrent streams) for infra to investigate.
noah: great, thanks everyone! :thumbsup:
